scope: Controlled direct-launch and diagnostic Release profiling; no application optimization or rendering change.
method: Same Release executable and DLLs, fresh isolated settings, 900x1000 window, 100% zoom, warm OS file cache, application PDBs hidden. PDFs passed on the process command line with -for-testing. Independent Bun monitor ready before spawn and attached 6-9 ms after it. First render idle, one-second settled memory, Cache Info pixel payload and one-second post-close memory recorded. Engine order alternated.
limits: Process start to render idle includes UI and control polling, not first paint or cold boot. CPU monitor misses the first 6-9 ms. Cache pixels are measured payload, not a complete allocation map; process Private Bytes include other SDK/UI/GDI/allocator state. Three qualifying pairs per PDF. Profile runs are diagnostic and excluded from performance medians.

gate.start: Three consecutive 1 s samples with busy CPU <=10% and OS memory load <=85%
gate.row: Other-CPU mean <=10%, p95 <=20% over 200 ms samples, OS memory load <=90%, monitor lag <=100 ms
gate.pair: Starting OS memory load within 3 percentage points
gate.exclusion: One IPA pair exceeded background-CPU p95; retry qualified

releaseProfile.note: Phase wall times include scheduling. Diagnostic logging is excluded from launch comparisons. First page may not be the first render thread to acquire the PDFium lock.

fontProbe.note: Standalone default-v1 callback diagnostic, not an application API trace. Font-info v2 changed alias pixels and remains rejected.

decision: First-use font enumeration is the leading startup cause for the two text PDFs; IPA shows no general PDFium startup penalty. Memory direction is document-dependent, and smaller PDFium tile payload does not explain text-PDF Private Bytes. Continue only font-lookup and allocation-ownership diagnosis. No cache-policy or font-rendering change approved.
next: Attribute post-visit non-pixel memory by SDK/UI/GDI allocation owner. Consider only a font-matching candidate that preserves application-rendered pixels for aliases and Japanese glyphs, with unchanged font selection, antialiasing, resolution and colors.
